synopsis: The Centre, day twenty. The crust goes brown and soft and forty-one hask stop dead in the traces, because two centuries have taught them that wet ground on the plain is the thing that kills you, and they are right about everything except this. Iseul Fane is at Benchmark One before them, having counted eleven stakes and read the numbers cut into them, and she asks Ysoly a second time what is on her way-bill and is not answered. Denet Rasca reopens bore nine, two hundred and forty paces east of the benchmark, and the College glass reads fresh in front of eleven witnesses and a Warden of the Third Rank; Hanei drinks and laughs before she can stop herself. Then the reversal: Denet has spent five months checking his own arithmetic hoping to find the mistake that would make it eighty feet, because eighty feet is a shaft, a windlass crew and a padlock, and a padlock has an owner who can be argued with. Nine feet is a spade and an afternoon and belongs to nobody, which means it cannot be sold, which means the four hundred blocks were never for the water. Ysoly works out why Oreth Vask stopped writing at the Dry Ferry and why his letter went north about her wagons; Pell Corrow goes quiet, does the sum, and says out loud that a debt written in blocks of salt is the one thing on the plain the water makes cheaper. Sennet reaches for the strict reading of the First Article and Denet closes it with his own auger logs -- salt to thirty-one inches at the thinnest, over the arm by any reckoning of the arm -- so the site is inside the bounds in the finder's own hand. Iseul recites the whole Fourth Article from memory, correctly, and then opens the waxed sleeve and reads it again, which she has not needed to do in four years. Ysoly rules: dig it, here, in front of the Warden, before the joint tile comes through on the twenty-fourth with two hundred people and spades of its own -- and dumps a hundred blocks of Assembly ballast onto the brown ground to buy back the day it costs, owed personally at the far rim. The hole is nine feet by the third hour of the morning and has two feet of water standing in it by the time the lamp burns down. At dawn Sabra Onn walks the pound and counts forty coughs where there were forty-one, drinks the first sweet water of her life that nobody carried, pours a full cup out on the ground on purpose, and then says the ration figure unchanged.
title: The Centre
